title: Response-Surface-Guided Extraction and Copper Modification of Nanocellulose from Corn Cob and Hemp Hurds: Source- and Loading-Dependent Structural and Electrochemical Properties
content: Nanocellulose was produced from hemp hurds and corn cob using a citric-acid-assisted chemical–mechanical route optimized by response surface methodology (RSM). Extraction cycle number and probe-sonication time were evaluated as process variables, with FTIR-derived total crystallinity index (TCI) and SEM-derived fibril size as responses. The selected conditions were 3 cycles/120 min for hemp hurds and 3 cycles/75 min for corn cob, yielding experimentally observed fibril sizes of 80 nm and 56.6 ± 8.8 nm, respectively. The optimized nanocelluloses were modified with nominal Cu loadings of 15, 25, 50, and 75 wt%. Cu incorporation reduced low-frequency impedance by more than 96% relative to bare nanocellulose and markedly increased cycle-5 passed charge, although the loading dependence differed between biomass sources. The 50 wt% formulations provided the most consistent combination of relatively low impedance and high passed charge across both sources. TGA revealed source-dependent increases in retained nonvolatile residue with Cu loading, while XRD confirmed face-centered cubic metallic Cu together with weaker cellulose-related reflections. The results demonstrate that extraction history and biomass source jointly govern nanocellulose structure and the electrochemical response to Cu modification.
